name: file-upload
description: File uploads through object storage: a single-request multipart endpoint and resumable chunked uploads whose state lives in the database, with downloads presigned only for the uploader or an administrator.
env: # file-upload: resumable chunked uploads. Largest file per upload, in bytes (1 GiB).
# Part size in bytes: at least 5 MiB and within API_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE (8 MiB).
# Seconds an unfinished upload may sit idle before it expires; each part restarts it.
# Seconds between sweeps that abort expired uploads on every replica; 0 turns it off.
# Part uploads per caller in each RATE_LIMIT_TTL window when rate-limit is installed.

inject.text:
### file-upload
- `POST /files` stores one multipart file under `uploads/<userId>/`; `GET /files/:key/url` presigns it for the owner or an administrator.
- For large files use the resumable upload in the browser: `uploadFile(file, { onProgress, signal })` and `resumeUpload(id, file)` from `$lib/uploads`. They create a session (`POST /files/uploads`), send parts (`PUT /files/uploads/:id/parts/:n`, `application/octet-stream`, `Content-Length` equal to the part size; with `XMLHttpRequest` in the browser so `onProgress` reports bytes), retry failed parts honoring `Retry-After`, and complete (`POST /files/uploads/:id/complete`). `GET /files/uploads/:id` lists stored parts; `DELETE` cancels.
- Upload sessions live in the database (`file_upload_sessions`, `file_upload_parts`), so any API replica serves any request; never keep upload state in memory. Run `{{apiRun}} migrate:all{{apiWorkspaceArg}}` after adding the module.
- Parts are larger than the web `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT`, so the gateway sends `/api/files/uploads/` straight to the API: `podo add` listed it in `.podokit/dev.json` `apiPaths` and each deployment profile's `exposure.apiPaths`, and `podo deploy init` adds it to new profiles. Keep it there.
- POST bodies must be `application/json` and parts `application/octet-stream` (else 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`), and a browser `Origin` outside `CORS_ORIGIN` gets 403. Branch on `error.code`: `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND`, `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `UPLOAD_PART_SIZE_MISMATCH`, `UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE`, `UPLOAD_COMPLETING`, `UPLOAD_EXPIRED`, `UPLOAD_ABORTED`.

instructions: Configure the selected object-storage provider before uploading files.
Run migrations to create the upload session tables: {{apiRun}} migrate:all{{apiWorkspaceArg}}
Uploads are stored as uploads/<userId>/<uuid>-<name>. Add the auth module so every upload has an owner.
Upload a file:  curl -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@./some.png' localhost:5002/files
The response includes { key, url } — an S3 presigned URL or a signed local download URL.
Presign it again (owner or administrator, key URL-encoded):  curl -b cookies.txt localhost:5002/files/uploads%2F<userId>%2F<file>/url
Uploads stored before per-user keys (uploads/<file>) can only be presigned by administrators.
Start a resumable upload:  curl -b cookies.txt -XPOST localhost:5002/files/uploads -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"filename":"big.bin","size":20000000}'
Send each part with its exact size:  curl -b cookies.txt -XPUT localhost:5002/files/uploads/<id>/parts/1 -H 'content-type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @part-1
Resume from GET /files/uploads/<id> (receivedParts), finish with POST /files/uploads/<id>/complete and '{}' as JSON, or cancel with DELETE /files/uploads/<id>.
In the browser, call uploadFile(file, { onProgress, signal }) or resumeUpload(id, file) from $lib/uploads.
Parts exceed the web server's BODY_SIZE_LIMIT, so they reach the API directly through /api/files/uploads/ (listed above as a direct API path). podo deploy init adds it to new deployment profiles.
